title: HOW WE KEEP YOU SAFE AT BRAINLYHQ?
excerpt: Your safety is one of our priorities at BrainlyHQ. We work to make sure you know who you can trust, where to ask for help, and how to recognize suspicious activity. From moderator verification to security updates and support channels, we want you to feel safe and informed while being part of our community.
body:
## Your Safety Comes First

BrainlyHQ is a community, and keeping that community safe requires clear rules and reliable ways to get help.

We continuously work on improving our security and making sure that members have access to the right information when something goes wrong. We also believe that **knowing how our security system works is just as important as the system itself**.

That is why we provide several ways for you to verify information, report problems, and contact the team safely.

## We Keep You Updated

When BrainlyHQ experiences a technical issue, maintenance, or temporary interruption, we keep the community informed.

Official information about technical breaks and important service updates is published through our official channels. If something suddenly stops working, **always check our official announcements before assuming that something is wrong with your account**.

> **Tip:** Be careful with messages claiming to be from BrainlyHQ staff during a technical issue. Always verify the source before clicking links or sharing information.

![](/assets/images/blog/scheduled.png)

## Moderators Will Never DM You First

This is one of the most important things to remember.

**BrainlyHQ moderators will never contact you privately first.** Moderators are also unable to reply to your private messages.

If someone sends you a DM claiming to be a BrainlyHQ moderator, administrator, or member of the security team, **do not assume that they are legitimate**.

Do not give them your:

- password
- verification codes
- account credentials
- private information
- payment information
- security codes

Instead, verify their identity through our official security system.

## Verify a Moderator Before Trusting Them

Think someone is a BrainlyHQ moderator? **Verify them first.**

You can use the **Verify Moderator** button available in the **Security** channel. This allows you to check whether the person you're dealing with is actually a member of the BrainlyHQ moderation team.

![](/assets/images/blog/verify.png)

If the verification does not match, stop communicating with the person and report the situation to the team.

**Never trust a role, username, profile picture, or nickname alone.** These can be copied or changed.

![](/assets/images/blog/successverify.png)

## Need Help? Use Our Support System

If you have a problem, question, or security concern, you don't need to find a moderator yourself.

BrainlyHQ provides an official **ticket and support system** where you can submit a request and receive assistance through the proper channels.

You can also use our **Help Form** to report an issue or ask for assistance.

**Help Form:** [Open the BrainlyHQ Help Form](https://forms.gle/1iLSiwES285HTczY8?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

For additional information and answers, you can use the official **BrainlyHQ Support & Knowledge Base**, which provides information about server rules, features, and other common questions.

[BrainlyHQ Support & Knowledge Base](https://discord.brainly.com/support.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

![](/assets/images/blog/tickets.png)

## A Few Simple Rules Can Keep You Safe

Most security problems can be avoided by following a few basic principles:

- Never share your passwords or verification codes.
- Never trust someone simply because they claim to be staff.
- Always verify moderators using the official Verify Moderator system.
- Use official BrainlyHQ support channels when you need help.
- Be suspicious of unexpected links, files, or requests for personal information.

And most importantly:

> **When in doubt, stop and verify.**

## We're Here to Help

Security is not only about preventing problems. It is also about making sure you know what to do when something doesn't feel right.

If you ever receive a suspicious message, encounter someone pretending to be a moderator, or simply aren't sure whether something is legitimate, **don't take unnecessary risks**. Use the official BrainlyHQ support system and let the team help you.

**Stay safe. Stay informed. And always verify before you trust.**
